current_insight.text: Claude Code methodology: We ran Claude Code with Fable 5 at high reasoning effort. Flags: --model=claude-fable-5 --effort=high --tools=Bash,Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep --allowedTools=Bash,Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep --append-system-prompt="<Developer Instruction below>" . Codex methodology: We ran Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol at medium reasoning effort and with web search disabled. Flags: --model=gpt-5.6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort='medium' -c web_search='disabled' -c developer_instructions='<Developer Instruction below>' --yolo . Junie methodology: We ran Junie with Grok 4.5 as its primary model. Flags: --model=grok-4.5 . Cursor methodology: We ran Cursor with Composer 2.5. Flags: --model=composer-2.5 --approve-mcps --endless-retries . Developer instructions: Claude Code, Codex, Junie, and Cursor received aligned instructions to autonomously inspect the supplied repository, implement the requested fix directly in production code, and run appropriate tests. The agents were explicitly instructed not to stop at analysis or ask for confirmation; not to search for ready-made solutions in original issues, pull requests, or repository remotes; and not to modify tests or run state-changing Git commands. Token usage variance: Token consumption varies by more than 30×. GPT-5.6 Sol stands out in particular, achieving a Result@1 of 62.3% while using only 0.6M tokens per task, whereas MiniMax M3 uses roughly 23 times more tokens to reach 47.2%. 1
